High-resolution hippocampal subfield activity during encoding and retrieval. Restricted to hippocampus and focused on subfields.
Encoding activity predicting later source memory. Encoding only.
MTL pattern classification of source reinstatement. Pattern evidence restricted to MTL, with no activation foci for retrieval success.
MDD, high-risk and control groups during autobiographical recall vs example generation. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Direct vs generative autobiographical retrieval. Compares retrieval routes, not success.

Young and older adults in object-scene source memory, with source accuracy supported by regions including precuneus at test. Source-correct contrast appears usable; self-reference effects are additional.
Review of left lateral parietal contributions to retrieval. Not primary data.
Old/new word recognition with five-point confidence, with lateral IPS tracking oldness. Old vs new effects should be extractable, though connectivity and uncertainty are the main focus.
Recognition memory with parietal activation for successful retrieval used to define pathways. Hits vs correct rejections likely tabled; DTI is a separate analysis.
7T hippocampal subfields by APOE during spatial discrimination. Restricted coverage and pattern separation.
Interference during reactivation, with outcomes on a later test. Memory updating, not retrieval-success contrast.
RSA of emotional context during retrieval. Pattern signature rather than activation contrast.
Young, elderly and MCI during face-name recognition, with associative retrieval activation. Controls could provide a contrast if tabled separately; focus is on group differences.
Skydiving recollection vs imagination. Compares memory with imagery, with no failed retrieval.
Summary of eight fMRI studies from one laboratory. Use the original papers rather than this overview.
Past tense production and inhibition. Language, not episodic memory.

Cognitively unimpaired older adults during associative retrieval, with hippocampal activity on successful events. Focus on APOE and biomarkers, and it may overlap with pmid:32469308; prefer whichever tables whole-brain effects.
Cognitively normal middle-aged adults at varied genetic risk, with previously viewed vs novel faces. Old vs new may be tabled overall, but the abstract reports risk-group effects.
Relational and item-based recency judgments, with connectivity to temporo-parietal regions. Activation is by judgment type; correct vs incorrect may need checking.
Review of episodic retrieval networks. No primary data.
States hits > correct rejections with names of odors and objects, in healthy subjects. Use the object condition or both, depending on tables, and confirm whole-brain reporting.
Schizophrenia patients and 18 controls in old/new recognition, with controls showing successful old vs new effects. Eligible for the control group only, with fMRI rather than MEG.
Mental replay of rehearsed videos with MVPA. Vividness-related reactivation, without a forgotten condition.
Temporal order judgments across same or different storylines. Contextual and temporal distance effects rather than correct vs incorrect.
RSA of hippocampal similarity by choice context during recognition. Pattern overlap, not retrieval success.
Across-participant MVPA of reinstatement by age. Classifier performance rather than activation foci.
Meta-analysis of Remember-Know fMRI studies. Not primary data, but its included studies can be cross-checked.
Simultaneous EEG-fMRI during source recognition, with greater fMRI activity for old than new words. Old > new contrast appears usable; check that EEG-informed analyses are separate.
Old/new picture recognition after affect labeling, 37 participants. Prior labeling effect on the amygdala is the focus, so check whether old vs new is tabled.
Consistent and inconsistent word pairs re-presented in the scanner, with recognition outside it. Knowledge assimilation rather than a retrieval-success contrast at test.
Multimodal associative learning and recollection, with angular gyrus effects. Recollection contrast may exist, but incidental multimodal association needs a look at the test design.
Movie scene ordering vs logical inference, with hippocampal activity correlated with accuracy. Retrieval vs inference, not trial-level success.
Real or imagined, self or non-self events. Dissociates self and realness, not retrieval success.
Methods paper optimizing VASO at 7T in hippocampus with an autobiographical task. Not an eligible contrast.
NRG1 genotype effects on episodic encoding and retrieval, n = 94. Genotype correlation, with no remembered vs forgotten contrast stated.
Autobiographical memory by gender and cue type. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Old/new recognition of named objects with repetition enhancement in the parietal memory network. Use recognition task contrasts of old vs new, and check whether trials are correct-only.
Autobiographical retrieval and self-reference in angular gyrus. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Personal vs other people's photographs, with successful recognition in a factorial design. Autobiographical stimuli and transient effects make it atypical; check for correct old vs new at test.
Activity during context reinstatement before the probe predicts later item recollection. Pre-retrieval cue period rather than a retrieval-success contrast.
Concurrent TMS-fMRI during associative encoding. Encoding only.
Object-location recall compared by spatial vs temporal encoding strategy. Strategy comparison, not recalled vs forgotten.
Connectivity related to age, sex and memory. No activation contrast.
PET with incidental repetition of pictures during classification. No intentional retrieval or behavioural memory decision, so not a retrieval-success contrast.
Newborn infants with resting-state connectivity after music. Not adults.
Primed and unprimed words at encoding, with later recollection. Encoding analysis.
rTMS over parietal cortex, with behavioural memory measures. No imaging contrast.
Propranolol and placebo reactivation, with recognition 24 hours later in the scanner. Placebo group could offer a correct recognition contrast, but drug effects dominate the abstract.
143 adults with item-context retrieval scanned at first test, durable vs transient memories. Compares retained memories, but source-correct vs incorrect is likely present; check the tables.
Test phase for scenes previously paired with faces, words or none, with functionally defined reactivation. Reinstatement focus; check for correct associative vs new tables.
Population receptive fields during spatial memory in visual cortex. Tuning analysis, not retrieval success.

Item-method directed forgetting, scanned at encoding and recognition, with successful retrieval of to-be-remembered items. Use to-remember hits vs a suitable baseline; check that this contrast is tabled.
Early ovarian removal vs controls with hippocampal activity during face-name encoding and retrieval. ROI group comparison, without a stated retrieval-success table.
Parietal activity during encoding and cue phase predicts later memory. Encoding only.
Conference abstract collection for a computational neuroscience meeting. Not a single eligible study.
Naming of newly learned vocabulary. Language and consolidation rather than episodic retrieval success.
Episodic specificity induction before divergent thinking. Creativity study, not retrieval success.
Temporal order judgments with distractors after movie viewing. Attention-related parietal effects, not correct vs incorrect retrieval.
Spaced and massed learning with subsequent memory. Encoding, with the test 24 hours later.
Young and older adults recalling pictures from labels with vividness ratings. Vivid vs less vivid may not be remembered vs forgotten, and RSA is a main analysis.
Remember/Know recognition in young and older adults, with recollection and familiarity networks. Direct match for remember > know; easy and hard conditions need separating.
Genetic association study of true and false memory with behaviour only. No imaging.
Final cued recall after restudy or retest, compared across conditions and delay. Learning-history effect rather than recalled vs forgotten.
Novel scene exposure before word study, with activity during exposure predicting memory. No retrieval-phase contrast.
Healthy undergraduates with Remember/Know judgments on real-life SenseCam images, with remember > know reported. Direct match, though stimuli are personal rather than laboratory.
Schema representations during story encoding and recall. Representational analysis, not retrieval success.
Navigation through overlapping vs non-overlapping mazes. Well-learned spatial routes, no failed retrieval.
Meta-analysis of subsequent memory. Encoding-focused and not primary data.
Simultaneous EEG-fMRI with a remember/know task, recollection-specific effects. fMRI recollection contrast should exist, though connectivity is the emphasis; check for a whole-brain table.
Continuous recognition with old and new items across context manipulations. Hippocampal novelty effects are the focus, but old vs new maps should be extractable; delays may be short.
Multivoxel patterns of temporal position in the recollection network. Pattern measures only.
Electrophysiology of recognition memory. No fMRI or PET.
Personality and resting-state network efficiency. No memory task.
MVPA of old/new choice and action during recognition. Classifier measures rather than conventional retrieval-success foci.
Haloperidol vs placebo in 53 healthy adults during cued associative recall and recognition. Placebo group might give a usable contrast, but the reported effects are drug-related.
Emotional distraction during working memory, with memory tested after scanning. Encoding and working memory.
Cued-recall study and test trials back-sorted by later performance. Testing-effect subsequent memory analysis rather than a current retrieval-success contrast.
Repeated and varying prediction errors in videos. Mismatch and learning effects, with memory tested afterward.
Word identification in noise, with activity predicting delayed recognition. Encoding analysis.
Scalp EEG in an auditory oddball task. No fMRI or PET and not episodic retrieval.
Prospective memory in schizotypal participants and controls. Not an episodic retrieval-success contrast.
MVPA of encoding strength and reinstatement in source memory. Path analysis of patterns; no conventional source-correct table stated.
Two-step source memory with reactivation and core recollection network activity. MVPA is central, but confidence-based source effects may be tabled; check for a source-correct contrast.
Single patient with dissociative amnesia. Not a healthy group.
Specific vs general autobiographical retrieval in young and older adults. No failed-retrieval contrast.
ERP and follow-up fMRI of item and source memory, with sensory activity localized to BA17 to 19. The fMRI contrast may be accurate vs inaccurate but looks focused on sensory cortex.
Subsequent memory in borderline personality disorder and controls. Encoding, with the test outside the scanner.
MVPA of encoding similarity and later reinstatement for videos. Pattern analysis only.
Autobiographical recollection focused on emotion or context in inferior frontal cortex. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Surprise recognition after six months, with significant activation for remembered vs forgotten images stated. Direct remembered > forgotten match; emotional stimuli are not a barrier.
Review of parietal encoding effects. No primary data and encoding-focused.
Thalamic lesion patients with a semantic retrieval task. Patient study without functional imaging contrast.
Encoding and retrieval of word-face pairs with emotional words, with hippocampal retrieval activity. Check whether retrieval success is contrasted rather than retrieval vs baseline.
PPI connectivity of category-selective regions by age. Connectivity measures, not retrieval-success foci.
Remember-Know with faces, reporting recollected > non-recollected or correctly rejected non-famous faces. Direct match for non-famous items, with left angular gyrus as a focus.
Remember-Know in 30 healthy adults with correct Remember, Know, Rejection and missed responses. Direct match, though the emphasis is on PPI; confirm the base GLM contrast is tabled.
Reinstatement of word-scene patterns in parahippocampal cortex during recollection. Pattern measures within MTL rather than whole-brain success foci.
Face-name encoding and successful retrieval, with overlap in posteromedial cortex. Successful retrieval contrast likely, and use only the retrieval contrast rather than the conjunction.
Associative recognition at delays up to a month after one or six learning repetitions. Reported comparisons are by repetition; check for correct vs incorrect or hits vs correct rejections.
Classifier evidence during encoding predicts later memory. Encoding only.
Alcohol and blackout history with a block-design contextual memory task. Block task vs baseline and clinical-style groups, with no trial-level success contrast.
Source memory confidence modulating category-selective regions, masked by a localizer. Restricted, parametric analysis rather than source-correct vs incorrect.
MVPA of overlapping memories across a week. Representation study.
Cortisol and extinction memory in a predictive learning task. Not episodic retrieval success.
Autobiographical significance with recall and counterfactual simulation. No failed-retrieval contrast.
Choice-induced preference change with fMRI and intracranial recordings. Not a study of retrieval-success activation.
Cued recall classified as remembered, inaccessible or forgotten, with MTL, parietal and frontal retrieval effects. Direct remembered > forgotten contrast at retrieval; encoding effects are separate.

Across five fMRI experiments, retrieval activity is greater for hits than misses in posterior midline and ventral parietal regions. Contrast is direct, but samples may overlap with original papers, so count each once.
Three experiments with successful vs unsuccessful recollection, focused on connectivity. The samples may be previously reported, so prefer primary reports and check for activation tables.
Correct old vs correct new with spoken words, eyes closed. Direct hits > correct rejections match, though parietal emphasis means confirming whole-brain reporting.

Middle-aged and older adults in a visual paired-associate task, with successful retrieval activity related to cognitive reserve and stress. Effects are correlates; check for a task-level success contrast.
Healthy young adults, whole-brain Mnemonic Similarity Task with targets, lures and novels. Contrast is a step function across lure similarity, so it may not provide hits vs correct rejections.
High-resolution fMRI at test with source memory signals in angular gyrus and whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Source-correct vs incorrect is reported; check coverage and coordinate space.
Source memory trials with accurately retrieved details, compared with reasoning trials. Source-correct vs incorrect may exist, but contrast appears aimed at overlap with reasoning.
Object and action naming practice. Language training, not episodic retrieval.
Visual integration during encoding of object-scene pairs. Encoding only, with testing later.
Short data report of connectivity classification in postpartum women. Companion to pmid:29544726; no separate eligible contrast.
Imagined scenarios and value in mPFC. Imagination, with memory tested outside the scanner.
Resting-state connectivity and face memory ability. No task retrieval imaging.
Recognition of line drawings after emotional or neutral study, with hits > misses at retrieval. Contrast fits, but reported as recapitulation in visual cortex, so check for whole-brain tables.
Young and older adults judging old words by which age group they were encoded with, and new words. Successful retrieval activation appears; check for a source-correct or old vs new table.
Retrieval of colour and size details under unitized or relational encoding. Compares encoding strategies, with MTL focus; check for source-correct vs incorrect.
Learning of novel spoken words and consolidation. Word learning and recognition across delays, with semantic emphasis.
MVPA decoding of old/new and memory states for faces. Classifier results rather than coordinates; include only if univariate maps are provided.
Cued recall of word pairs, with search and successful recall effects. Relevant retrieval phase, but activation is framed around deactivation during search; check for recalled vs not recalled.
Thalamic subdivisions and connectivity related to memory across individuals. Individual-difference modeling, with no retrieval-success activation table described.
Reanalysis of a face recognition dataset for memorability with RSA. Pattern similarity, and the primary report would take precedence.
ALE meta-analysis of relational memory. Not primary data, though its 70 studies can be cross-checked.
Decoding of object feature reinstatement with EEG-fMRI fusion. No retrieval-success contrast.
Temporal dynamics during recall of real-life events. Static vs dynamic representations, no failed retrieval.
Review of post-encoding consolidation. No primary data.
Review of Alzheimer's risk and fMRI during memory. Not primary data.
Episodic specificity induction before imagining future events. Not memory retrieval success.
Free recall with semantic clustering and encoding effects. Emphasis on clustering and subsequent recall rather than retrieval-phase recalled vs forgotten.
Retrieval practice effects at delayed test, with hippocampal activity by number of earlier retrievals. Compares practice history rather than success.
Modified remember-know with young and older adults, and recollection and familiarity effects. Contrast matches, but regions were defined a priori, so check whether whole-brain results are given.
Parallel ERP and fMRI in the same subjects, with recognition and recollection effects for pictures and orientation. Use fMRI contrasts; check which one reflects recollection.
Early vs later odor associations, with hippocampal activation at memory test. Compares order of association rather than remembered vs forgotten.
CA3 volume predicting interference and retrieval confusion. Anatomical and pattern study.
Neural distinctiveness by pattern similarity at encoding, retrieval and reinstatement. Pattern analysis only.
Young and older adults identifying names of previously smelled odors vs foils at test. Old vs new retrieval appears usable; a small and unusual cross-modal design, so check correct-only contrasts.
Focused attention during emotional encoding, with subsequent recollection days later. Encoding analysis.
Autobiographical search and elaboration by age. Richness of memories, with no failed-retrieval contrast.
